project.name: Tank Siege
project.description: Tank Siege is a browser-based top-down tank shooter inspired by the browser classic Awesome Tanks 2. Players pilot an upgradeable tank through escalating waves of AI-controlled enemy tanks and turrets, earning coins and XP from kills to unlock weapons, armor, and mobility upgrades. The game targets the same fast, arcade-y, one-more-wave loop as the original, rebuilt as a modern responsive web app playable on desktop and mobile browsers with a persistent meta-progression economy.
project.backend: Lightweight cloud save + leaderboard service (player profile, coin balance, unlock state, wave high scores), hosted as a thin web API/BaaS, with client-authoritative gameplay and server-validated economy transactions to prevent coin tampering.
project.stack_decision: Browser-based web game stack (e.g. HTML5 Canvas/WebGL via a JS/TS game framework such as Phaser or PixiJS) with a thin backend (managed BaaS or lightweight API) for save sync and anti-cheat validation of coin balances.
project.market_decision: Free-to-play browser-based arcade/casual market, monetized via optional ads and cosmetic/convenience purchases through a web payment provider; the core coin economy (including the God Gun) remains earn-only to preserve skill/grind progression rather than pay-to-win.

coin_economy.earn_sources: Enemy kills, wave-clear bonuses, daily login bonus, mission rewards
coin_economy.rationale: Coins are earn-only so that high-cost unlocks like the God Gun remain a grind-based prestige reward rather than a pay-to-win purchase

god_gun.cooldown: none (single-use consumable, must be re-purchased for 1,000,000 coins each use)

phase_0.summary: Project has not yet started implementation; this PRD represents the initial planned scope.

next_planned_features.title: US-2.1 — God Gun purchase and instant-defeat weapon
next_planned_features.rationale: The God Gun is the signature high-end progression reward that gives long-term players a coin sink and a satisfying end-game power fantasy; it depends on the core coin economy and combat loop already existing.

strategy_pivot.supersedes: v1 (adopted 2026-09-04) — the native mobile app (iOS + Android) platform and distribution decision. Core gameplay scope (epic-1, epic-2), personas, and coin economy policies from v1 are unchanged.
strategy_pivot.rationale: Pivoting from a native mobile app (iOS + Android) to a browser-based web game to avoid App Store/Play Store review friction and the platform fee cut, and to enable instant updates without app store release cycles.

architecture_change.distribution: Native mobile app (iOS + Android) -> browser-based web app (HTML5/WebGL, desktop + mobile-responsive)

commercial_model.primary: Free-to-play with optional rewarded/interstitial ads and cosmetic purchases (skins, tank paint jobs)
commercial_model.free_tier: Full core game (all waves, all coin-earned upgrades including the God Gun) is playable without spending money
commercial_model.refund_policy: Standard refund terms via the web payment provider (e.g. Stripe) for cosmetic purchases; no refunds on consumed in-game coins
commercial_model.subscription_trigger: Not planned for MVP; revisit if a cosmetic-only battle pass shows demand post-launch
commercial_model.break_even: n/a for MVP — success measured on retention and engagement metrics before monetization scale-up

phases.name: Core Gameplay Prototype
phases.precondition: Web game framework and hosting scaffolding selected

criteria: Core loop is fun in internal playtest
60fps on mid-tier target devices in supported browsers
gate.decision_if_failed: Revisit control scheme or performance budget before continuing

operating_constraints.team: Small indie team (2-4 people) + AI-assisted development

target_markets.name: United States
target_markets.notes: Primary launch market; standard web accessibility and data-privacy compliance (e.g. CCPA), COPPA-aware design since arcade shooters attract younger players.

target_markets.name: Global English-speaking markets (UK, Canada, Australia, etc.)
target_markets.notes: Same build as US market; no additional localization required for initial launch.

personas.name: Casey the Casual Grinder
personas.description: Plays in short 5-10 minute mobile sessions during downtime. Wants quick, satisfying wave-clear runs and steady visible progress on upgrades. Cares about session length fitting a commute, and about coin balance feeling like it's always going somewhere useful.

personas.name: Val the Completionist Veteran
personas.description: Has played for weeks, cleared most standard upgrades, and is actively grinding toward big-ticket unlocks like the 1,000,000-coin God Gun. Cares about long-term goals, leaderboard standing, and having a satisfying 'end-game' power fantasy to work toward.

requirements: Gameplay economy logic (coin balance, deductions, God Gun purchase) must have automated unit tests covering success and insufficient-funds paths
Combat/damage resolution (including instant-defeat effects) must have automated tests verifying correct target elimination and no unintended side effects on other enemies

delivery.branching: Feature branches off main, merged via PR
delivery.release: Staged web rollout via feature flags / percentage-based canary deploys behind a CDN

success_metrics.name: Day 1 Retention
success_metrics.definition: Percentage of new players that return to play again on the calendar day after their first session

success_metrics.name: Day 7 Retention
success_metrics.definition: Percentage of new players that return to play again 7 days after their first session

success_metrics.name: God Gun Redemption Rate
success_metrics.definition: Percentage of players still active at day 30 who have accumulated and spent 1,000,000 coins on a God Gun at least once

slos.target: ≥ 60fps on mid-tier target devices (released within last 3 years)
slos.error_budget: Frame drops below 45fps in < 1% of session time

epics.name: Core Combat & Progression
epics.description: The foundational gameplay loop: tank movement and shooting, AI enemy waves, coin drops on kills, and a coin-driven upgrade shop for weapons/armor/mobility. This scaffolding is a prerequisite for the God Gun to have coins, enemies, and combat to act on.

user_stories.title: Basic tank movement and shooting
user_stories.description: As a player, I want to move my tank and fire its cannon using touch controls, so that I can engage enemies in combat.

acceptance_criteria.description: Player can move the tank in any direction using an on-screen virtual joystick

aaa.arrange: Player is on the wave-survival screen with a tank spawned at the starting position
aaa.act: Player drags the on-screen movement joystick in a given direction
aaa.assert: Tank moves smoothly in that direction at the defined movement speed

acceptance_criteria.description: Player can aim and fire the tank's cannon independently of movement

aaa.arrange: Player's tank is active on screen with at least one enemy visible
aaa.act: Player drags the on-screen aim/fire control toward an enemy and releases
aaa.assert: A projectile fires from the tank toward the aimed direction and can damage an enemy on hit

user_stories.title: Wave-based enemy spawning
user_stories.description: As a player, I want enemy tanks to spawn in escalating waves, so that the game continually challenges me and gives me a sense of progression within a run.

acceptance_criteria.description: Each wave spawns a defined set of enemies that scales in count and/or difficulty as waves progress

aaa.arrange: Player starts a new run at wave 1
aaa.act: Player clears all enemies in wave 1
aaa.assert: Wave 2 spawns with an equal or greater number/difficulty of enemies than wave 1

user_stories.title: Coin drops and persistent coin balance
user_stories.description: As a player, I want to earn coins from defeating enemies and keep that balance saved between sessions, so that I can accumulate enough currency to afford upgrades and high-cost items like the God Gun.

acceptance_criteria.description: Defeating an enemy adds a defined coin amount to the player's balance

aaa.arrange: Player's coin balance is at a known value N and an enemy with a known coin reward R is on screen
aaa.assert: Player's coin balance becomes N + R

acceptance_criteria.description: Coin balance persists across app restarts via cloud/local save

aaa.arrange: Player has a coin balance of N and closes the app
aaa.assert: Player's coin balance is still N

user_stories.title: Upgrade shop for weapons, armor, and mobility
user_stories.description: As a player, I want to spend coins in an upgrade shop to buy and equip weapon, armor, and mobility upgrades for my tank, so that I feel steady, visible progress between wave runs.

acceptance_criteria.description: Player can view available weapon, armor, and mobility upgrades along with their coin cost and current owned/equipped state

aaa.arrange: Player has a known coin balance and opens the upgrade shop
aaa.act: Player browses the weapon, armor, and mobility upgrade lists
aaa.assert: Each upgrade displays its coin cost, a description, and whether it is currently owned and/or equipped

acceptance_criteria.description: Purchasing an upgrade deducts its coin cost from the player's balance and unlocks it permanently

aaa.arrange: Player's coin balance is at least the cost C of an unowned upgrade
aaa.assert: Player's coin balance decreases by exactly C and the upgrade is marked owned and persists across app restarts

acceptance_criteria.description: An upgrade cannot be purchased if the player has insufficient coins

aaa.arrange: Player's coin balance is less than the cost C of an unowned upgrade
aaa.act: Player attempts to purchase that upgrade
aaa.assert: The purchase is blocked or disabled, no coins are deducted, and the upgrade remains locked

acceptance_criteria.description: Player can equip one owned upgrade per slot (weapon, armor, mobility) and the equipped upgrade takes effect in the next run

aaa.arrange: Player owns more than one upgrade in a single slot category (e.g. two weapon upgrades)
aaa.act: Player selects and equips one of the owned upgrades in that slot
aaa.assert: That upgrade becomes the active one for the slot, and its effect (e.g. weapon fire pattern, damage mitigation, movement speed) applies starting with the player's next run

implementation.notes: Depends on persistent coin balance (US-1.3). Upgrade effects (weapon fire patterns, armor damage mitigation, mobility speed) should be defined in a shared config/data table rather than hardcoded, to keep balancing changes low-risk.

epics.name: God Gun
epics.description: A premium, coin-gated weapon that instantly defeats a single targeted enemy. Serves as the game's headline high-end coin sink and end-game power fantasy for highly engaged players, while remaining earn-only so it never becomes pay-to-win.

user_stories.title: Purchase and fire the God Gun
user_stories.description: As a player, I want to spend 1,000,000 coins to fire a God Gun so that I can instantly defeat a tough enemy.

acceptance_criteria.description: Firing the God Gun costs exactly 1,000,000 coins, deducted from the player's balance at the moment of use

aaa.arrange: Player's coin balance is at least 1,000,000 and a valid enemy target is on screen
aaa.act: Player selects the God Gun, targets an enemy, and confirms
aaa.assert: Player's coin balance decreases by exactly 1,000,000

acceptance_criteria.description: Firing the God Gun instantly defeats the targeted enemy regardless of its remaining health

aaa.arrange: An enemy with full health (including a high-health enemy type) is targeted and player has sufficient coins
aaa.act: Player fires the God Gun at that enemy
aaa.assert: The targeted enemy is immediately removed/defeated in a single hit, independent of its health value

acceptance_criteria.description: The God Gun cannot be activated if the player has fewer than 1,000,000 coins

aaa.arrange: Player's coin balance is less than 1,000,000
aaa.act: Player attempts to select/fire the God Gun
aaa.assert: The God Gun option is disabled or the fire action is blocked, and no coins are deducted

acceptance_criteria.description: Player must confirm the purchase via an explicit confirmation prompt before the coins are spent, given the high cost

aaa.arrange: Player has sufficient coins and selects the God Gun to fire at a target
aaa.assert: A confirmation prompt displaying the 1,000,000 coin cost appears before any coins are deducted or damage is applied; canceling the prompt spends no coins and defeats no enemy

acceptance_criteria.description: The God Gun does not instantly defeat boss enemies (open design decision: bosses are explicitly excluded from the instant-defeat effect for balance reasons, per project policy god_gun.applies_to_bosses)

aaa.arrange: A boss-type enemy is on screen and player has sufficient coins
aaa.act: Player attempts to target the boss with the God Gun
aaa.assert: The God Gun is either not targetable at the boss or fires without instantly defeating it, and no coins are deducted if the action is blocked

implementation.notes: Depends on core combat (US-1.1) and coin balance (US-1.3) already being implemented. Whether the God Gun excludes bosses is a product decision captured in project.policies.god_gun and should be revisited with design/playtesting before final lock.

epics.name: PvP Multiplayer Arena
epics.description: Real-time or asynchronous player-vs-player tank combat mode. Deferred until the core PvE wave-survival game has proven retention and revenue, since it introduces matchmaking, latency-sensitive netcode, and competitive balance considerations distinct from the wave-survival core loop.

epics.name: Clan & Social Features
epics.description: Player clans/guilds, friends lists, and social features such as clan leaderboards and gifting, aimed at driving long-term retention and virality. Deferred post-revenue since it requires a mature player base and additional backend infrastructure (social graph, clan chat) beyond MVP scope.
